title: elitedesk X520 LAN port dropped off PCIe
description: At 2026-11-18 17:13:33 EST, ~2.5 h after boot, the kernel logged 'ixgbe 0000:01:00.1: Adapter removed' and 'firmware error detected FWSM: 0xFFFFFFFF'; enp1s0f1 (LAN, DAC) lost carrier. No AER or thermal messages. Driver rebind and PCI FLR both failed (probe error -5); a warm reboot restored the port at 10 Gb/s. A router whose LAN NIC can vanish is not fit to be primary. Investigate: card temperature and airflow (X520s run hot in small chassis), PCIe ASPM (try pcie_aspm=off), slot seating, firmware; add a Prometheus alert for ixgbe 'Adapter removed' and link loss; watch for recurrence over a multi-day soak. Acceptance: root cause or mitigation applied, plus 7 days without recurrence before elitedesk becomes primary.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text: Recurred 2026-11-19 22:13:07 EST (about 45.5 h after the 00:38 boot): 'ixgbe 0000:01:00.1: Adapter removed', 'firmware error detected FWSM: 0xFFFFFFFF'; port 0 (WAN, 01:00.0) removed at 22:14:41. Found 2026-11-20 15:45: enp1s0f1 still NO-CARRIER, both ports gone, eno1 (mgmt) fine. E15 soak (dns-soak-atr-on-long) saw 100% UDP+TCP failure from 22:13 to its end (n=37666, 1967 each). Per the discussion-21 gate, a recurrence means swapping the X520 for the ConnectX-4 Lx and re-running the gate; left the box untouched (no reboot) for diagnosis.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text: 2026-11-20: X520 replaced by ConnectX-4 Lx MCX4121A-ACAT (ex-Huawei, stock PSID MT_2420110034), firmware updated 14.26.4012 -> 14.32.1912 (backups in emerald:~/nic-firmware-backups), moved to the CPU x16 slot: link 8GT/s x8 (was 5GT/s x4 on the PCH slot). Deployed (PR #23): LAN enp1s0f0np0 up at 10G with 10.10.10.4. 24 h gate started 18:00 EST: unit gate-cx4 on elitedesk (elitedesk->router TCP+UDP 1/s, hourly SNAP with carrier changes, PHY error counters, chip temp, kernel AER/mlx5 events, zone serial primary vs secondary) and user unit gate-cx4-reverse on emerald (emerald->elitedesk TCP+UDP 1/s). Ends about 2026-11-21 18:00. Note: card now advertises ASPM L1; if any link event appears, try pcie_aspm=off first.

title: Upstream: router.monitoring rules must not use services.prometheus.rules
description: nix-router-optimized monitoring.nix adds its alert group as a JSON string to services.prometheus.rules. Acceptance: upstream PR merged; consumers can use either option.

title: elitedesk X520 loses TCP replies (Flow Director ATR suspected)
description:
Found 2026-11-19 in the zoneReplication.ha rehearsal. Symptom: ~3.6% of TCP DNS queries from elitedesk to router 10.10.10.1:53 time out (18/504 over 10 min); UDP 0/504; emerald 0/1170 over TCP+UDP in the same window. Packet capture on elitedesk: router never answers the SYN (neither the ECN SYN nor the plain retry); 13/14 other ECN SYNs were answered, so ECN is not the cause, and the source port was not reused. Router-side listen overflows were disproven as the cause (round 1): they belong to router-dashboard :8888 (nch-sny.35). Impact: zone transfers (TCP), DoT/large answers, and the HA SOA check (now retried 3x, nix-router-optimized#149) -- a real failover risk.

Test plan (each round recorded here):
1. Attribute: which process/listener overflows (ss -ltn Recv-Q sampling, nstat deltas per minute), which clients open TCP :53 most (conntrack by src), and whether bursts line up with Technitium tasks (blocklist update, zone transfer, stats).
2. Reproduce on demand: parallel TCP query load from a LAN host; compare elitedesk vs emerald vs a third host; vary ECN on/off.
3. Fix candidates: raise the listen backlog (net.core.somaxconn and Technitium's TCP backlog/accept settings), tune Technitium TCP options, check router CPU/thread starvation; one change at a time.
4. Verify: overnight probe from >=2 hosts over TCP and UDP plus AXFR, zero timeouts; overflows on the :53 listener zero (bpftrace per-port; the host-wide counter includes router-dashboard :8888, tracked in nch-sny.35); repeat on elitedesk as the DNS server before any failover.
Acceptance: root cause named, fix deployed, round 4 clean on both routers.

Pass/fail gate (discussion 21): before VRRP is enabled or elitedesk is promoted, a 24 h probe from elitedesk to router and from another LAN host to elitedesk (TCP and UDP, 1 query/s each, plus hourly AXFR) must show zero TCP reply losses, no ixgbe 'Adapter removed', no AER errors and no unexpected carrier changes. Any recurrence means swapping the X520 for the ConnectX-4 Lx and re-running the gate.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text:
Round 1 (2026-11-19, attribution), corrects the hypothesis in the description:
- Router's ListenOverflows come from router-dashboard :8888 (backlog 5), shown with a bpftrace kprobe on tcp_conn_request; :53 never filled. That's a separate small bug.
- Simultaneous captures on router (any iface) and elitedesk (-i any): for every failed connection router received the SYN and sent SYN-ACK out enp6s16, retransmitting 6+ times over 16 s. elitedesk received none of them on any interface. Other connections in the same seconds worked.
- Not deterministic per 4-tuple: reusing the failed source ports later always succeeded. UDP never fails, and emerald never fails.
- Suspect: X520/82599 Flow Director ATR (hashes TCP flows; UDP RSS ignores ports). This driver has no flow-director-atr priv flag; ntuple on disables ATR.
- A/B so far is inconclusive: ATR off gave 0/400 and 0/400, but the ATR-on control also gave 0/400; earlier ATR-on runs failed 1-8%. Toggling ntuple may flush a stale fdir table.
- Running: 2 h TCP+UDP soak on elitedesk with ntuple on (unit dns-soak-atr-off, runtime-only setting).
Next rounds: (2) 2 h soak with ATR on as control; (3) a third LAN host and switch-port/cable check, ruling out the switch; (4) if ATR is confirmed, persist ntuple on (or a module option) and verify overnight on both TCP and UDP plus AXFR.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text: E15 (12 h ATR-on control) is void for ATR: from 22:13 the whole X520 dropped off PCIe (nch-sny.31 recurrence), so every query failed. Before 22:13 the only failures were the known 21:30-21:35 outage window (10 TCP, 10 UDP, both protocols, so not ATR). If the X520 is replaced by the ConnectX-4 Lx, the ATR question becomes moot; re-run the 24 h gate on the new NIC.

title: router-dashboard listen backlog of 5 overflows
description: Found in nch-sny.34 round 1: a bpftrace kprobe on tcp_conn_request showed router-dashboard :8888 with a full accept queue (q=5/5, then 6/5); it accounts for router's TcpExtListenOverflows (~7/min, 143k since boot). The dashboard is Python http.server with the default request_queue_size of 5. Fix upstream in nix-router-optimized (larger request_queue_size, or a threaded server). Acceptance: no full-queue hits on :8888 over an hour of normal polling.

title: Supervised router failover rehearsal (router <-> elitedesk)
description: From discussion 21 (nix-router-optimized docs/discussions/21). Write a runbook: console access, abort criteria, measured outage (WAN DHCP lease, IPv6 prefix, DNS, DHCP, zone promotion), alert expectations (ntfy/watchdog), and a tested fail-back. Run one supervised manual promotion before enabling VRRP, then one VRRP drill. Upgrade one node at a time, backup first; do not assume magic rollback for clan machines update. Acceptance: runbook in docs/router-failover.md, results recorded, failback proven.

title: Home port: herdr-core for the herdr mobile apps (hc, autostart unit, linger)
description:
herdr mobile apps (official iOS/Android client) connect over SSH to herdr-core (`hc connect`), not to the herdr TUI. unified got this working on emerald/phoenix in PR #239, commit e3863895 and PR #242; the generic port of common/herdr.nix in nch-sny.37.4 can easily drop it. Port:
- herdr-core package (overlay `herdr-core` from the separate `llm-agents-herdr-app` input, which also pins herdr-app; add it to the nch-sny.37.2 input list).
- programs.herdr.core.enable (default = desktopApp.enable) and core.autostart: a user oneshot unit running `hc server start`, WantedBy default.target.
- Already present here, just confirm: users.users.deepwatrcreatur.linger on workstations (modules/_nixos/workstation.nix) and custom.fishInteractiveShell via nixos-base. A fish login shell makes POSIX probes over SSH fail, so the app reports "herdr is not installed".
Acceptance: on clan-spike (or the migrated host), with a fresh SSH session with ControlPath=none, `ssh host 'if command -v hc >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo FOUND; fi'` prints FOUND; `systemctl --user is-active herdr-core` is active after boot with no login; the herdr iOS app connects and lists the host terminals.
Note: the herdr TUI runs its own server and its sessions never show in the mobile app (upstream design); only hc and herdr-app terminals do.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text: herdr-mobile SSH keys are not in Nix yet. The herdr iOS app added two keys, comment 'herdr-mobile' (SHA256:qDeo3QmvJmMuSrxTovIlOCgaW7IZ3xHHHIutOH8CGwg and SHA256:aD5OdLlYJXGIbMsn4UTnsGSWz94aakgu7e03P3lzYOk), to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on emerald and phoenix (a plain file, written about 2026-11-09/10). They are not in either repo, so a reinstall or the clan-migrated hosts lose phone access. Copy the public keys from either host's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys into keys/ (for example keys/herdr-mobile-*.pub) and add them to deepwatrcreatur's openssh.authorizedKeys.keyFiles on the hosts the app should reach (modules/aspects/deepwatrcreatur.nix). Ask the operator first whether both keys are still in use: two keys suggests two devices or an app reinstall. Acceptance: the app connects to the migrated host with ~/.ssh/authorized_keys absent.

title: Home port: GitHub SSH transport and signing key (pin, verify against GitHub)
description:
On 2026-11-21 GitHub SSH push and commit verification broke on emerald. unified pins github.com to ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 with IdentitiesOnly (modules/home-manager/ssh-agent.nix), and git signs with the same key (user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub). That key is keys/deepwatrcreatur-phoenix.pub here (SHA256:6DrmID...), and it had been removed from the GitHub account. The only GitHub-accepted key left in the agent was MP9Wt..., which unified mislabels as ssh-keys/root@pve-gateway-ed25519.pub (pve-gateway is now elitedesk, reinstalled as NixOS). Its private half exists only in emerald's running ssh-agent.
When nch-sny.37.3 ports ssh-agent/git-ssh-signing:
- pin github.com (IdentityFile + IdentitiesOnly) and user.signingkey to the key in keys/deepwatrcreatur-phoenix.pub, named in one place. Consider renaming the file, since it is the operator key on emerald and phoenix, not phoenix-only.
- port unified's scripts/git-ssh-doctor.sh, or an equivalent check.
- do not import ssh-keys/root@pve-gateway-ed25519.pub or any other retired-host key.
Acceptance: on the migrated host, `ssh -T -o BatchMode=yes git@github.com` authenticates; `gh api repos/<repo>/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.verified` is true for a fresh signed commit; git-ssh-doctor reports no failures.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text: Live state resolved 2026-11-21: the operator re-registered keys/deepwatrcreatur-phoenix.pub (SHA256:6DrmID...) on GitHub as both an authentication and a signing key, and removed the retired pve-gateway key (SHA256:MP9Wt...). On emerald, ssh -T git@github.com authenticates, signed commits verify on GitHub, and unified's git-ssh-doctor reports 8 ok / 0 fail. Nothing is broken now; this bead stays open for the port requirements only.

title: Spike: deploy and rollback behaviour (clan machines update vs deploy-rs)
description: Deploy a change with clan machines update. Then deploy a change that breaks SSH/network and record what happens. Acceptance: written comparison with deploy-rs magic rollback; decision on what the routers use.
close_reason: clan update has no rollback (broken gen becomes boot default); deploy-rs magic rollback works on clan machines once a deploy-rs generation exists. Routers -> deploy-rs. docs/plan.md#nch-sny5-deploy-and-rollback-done
